sent_to_model:
I need a letter for my guy Kelechi, abeg. Long story, at my birthday he was moaning about his job again (quantity surveyor, 9 years, bored to death) and I said he should come and teach maths. He laughed and said if I'm serious I should put it in writing, a proper letter, not voice note, and he will read it on the train. So I want to actually convince him. Not preach, he hates being preached to. We've been friends since Unilag. I will print it and post it to him in Croydon, he will think it's funny that I posted it. My points are below, use what works. Applications for next September open soon so I want him to at least go to the open evening on 19 November.

- Kelechi Obi, 34, quantity surveyor at a firm in Croydon, been there 9 yrs, says every day is the same spreadsheet
- he got A in further maths, he was the one tutoring half our hostel in Moremi before exams
- our school (Peckham, 1100 kids) has had a supply teacher covering two Year 9 maths groups since September
- training route is the salaried one, he gets paid while training, one year, starts September 2027
- open evening Thursday 19 November 2026, 6pm, at the training partnership in Lewisham, I can go with him
- pay drop first year yes, but holidays, pension, and it goes up
- last month a Year 11 boy, Damola, finally got simultaneous equations after 3 weeks, he shouted 'is that all??' and the whole class clapped
- Kelechi helped my nephew with fractions at Christmas using jollof rice portions on plates, nephew still talks about it
- when I started in 2019 I cried in the car park twice in first term, I'm not hiding that, it gets better
- on his last birthday he said 'I just want to do something that matters before 40'
- he is patient and funny, kids would love him, he explains things without making you feel stupid
- teaching is hard, marking is endless, behaviour some days is wahala, I won't lie to him
- he's not too old, a woman in my department started at 41
- he is wasting himself checking other people's costings
- convince him to at least come to the open evening, not sign anything yet
- honest about the bad parts, otherwise he won't believe the good parts
- a bit of teasing, the way we talk

(About me: secondary-school maths teacher, 33, Peckham, London. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Makes the case for Kelechi to become a maths teacher using his experience and teaching ability.
Acknowledges the difficult parts of teaching and the initial pay drop.
Asks him to attend the open evening on 19 November as an exploratory visit before any decision to sign up or change careers.
